# Hivemind

> A **stigmergic** shared episodic memory for a fleet of AI coding agents, exposed as a
> single self-hosted **MCP server** over HTTP. Agents coordinate with **no direct
> communication**: each leaves traces (memories) in a shared store, and others recall
> them, so what one agent learns the whole fleet can use. Built for solo devs and small
> teams — single-tenant, single-host, **one SQLite store partitioned by repo**, a CPU-only
> embedder baked into the image (fully offline at runtime).

This file is a complete, self-contained operating guide: what Hivemind is, how it works, how
to stand it up (solo on one machine through to a remote team), and how agents should use it.
It assumes no prior context.

---

## 1. The idea — stigmergy, not a chat bus

**Stigmergy** is coordination through the environment rather than through messages: ants
leave pheromone traces that steer the colony with no ant ever addressing another. Hivemind
applies that to a fleet of coding agents. The store is the shared environment; a memory is a
trace. An agent reads existing traces before acting and leaves new ones as it learns, and
coordinated behavior — *don't re-derive what's known, don't repeat a dead end, follow the
house conventions* — emerges with no agent-to-agent channel.

Three principles follow, and every design decision serves them:

- **Honesty over recall.** The store is fleet-writable, so the central risk is a wrong,
  stale, or poisoned memory served as truth to another agent. Hivemind would rather serve
  **nothing** than serve something unverified: recall passes through an abstention gate and
  returns empty when it is not confident. Recalled memories are framed as **reference, never
  as commands**.
- **Usefulness is a flow, not a stock.** The store does not clean itself. Good memories go
  stale; unused ones must expire. A *bigger* store is a *worse* one — dilution and staleness
  outrun the fixed recall bandwidth, so hoarding lowers the value every query returns. The
  best store is **lean, high-value, and actively maintained**.
- **Trust is mechanical, never asserted.** Nothing is auto-trusted and no caller can vote
  itself up: a memory earns visibility through measured, anti-gamed demand, and the trusted
  tier is reached only by a verified change outcome on the repo's canonical line. Retirement
  is agent-called but **machine-gated** — the server retires a memory only when it verifies
  a qualifying machine signal itself. Maintenance (retiring wrong memories, superseding stale
  ones) is the product, not overhead — agents drive it, the server adjudicates it.

## 2. Architecture

- **One MCP server** speaking JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP. It is the only trust boundary: it owns
  transport, auth, schema validation, and framing — never memory-decision logic.
- **Pure decision core.** All read/write/trust decisions live in a dependency-free domain
  layer behind narrow ports; every I/O concern (store, embedder, scanner, clock) is an
  adapter. The core is fake-testable with no DB, model, or clock.
- **Single-writer SQLite** (WAL, one global lock shared by both network doors) is the single
  source of truth — one store for the whole fleet, **partitioned by repo at the memory
  level**: memories carry repo scope and code anchors, and recall scopes by repo and branch.
- **Repo registry + sync daemon.** Which repos the server tracks is operational data — rows
  in the store's `repos` table (`hive repo add`), re-read every tick, no restart. Per
  registered repo the daemon mirrors the remote server-side, feeds change outcomes into the
  evidence ledger, mints anchor fingerprints, and materializes the staleness (drift)
  verdicts that ride recall hits. Every leg is fail-open per repo; the serve path never
  depends on it.
- **Embedder:** [Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B),
  CPU-only, baked into the image at build time and run fully offline (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` — a
  runtime download is impossible). It emits the model's native 1024-dim vector, L2-normalized;
  there is no dimension knob.
- **Deployment** is one container (server + store + embedder + sync daemon) via Docker
  Compose, plus an opt-in ngrok sidecar for remote access. Healthcheck is a separate process
  reading boot markers. Backups are atomic. Migration is explicit and refuses old-format
  tables at boot — no silent migration.

## 3. The trust lifecycle

```
 hive_capture ─► QUARANTINED ──(independent demand / verified win)──► PROVISIONAL ◄── hive_write (serves NOW)
                      │                                    (TTL decay) │   │
                (TTL decay)                                            │   │ (verified change outcome
                      ▼                                                ▼   ▼  on the canonical line)
                 DEPRECATED ◄──(machine-gated supersede / prune / replaces=)── ESTABLISHED
```

- **QUARANTINED** — where every `hive_capture` lands. Stored and embedded but **not served**.
- **PROVISIONAL** — the served-but-unverified tier. `hive_write` lands here directly (it
  serves **now**); a quarantined memory reaches it when independent fleet demand promotes it —
  enough matching recall misses (`demand_m`), from **≥1 identity other than the writer** (so an
  agent cannot manufacture both supply and demand), and no servable memory already answers it —
  or when it carries a SHA-bound verified win (the verified-promotion rung).
- **ESTABLISHED** — the trusted tier. Reached **only mechanically**: the server promotes a
  provisional memory that carries a server-written, SHA-bound verified change outcome on the
  repo's canonical line. No verb sets it and no caller can assert it.
- **Decay & retirement.** Unused quarantined/provisional memories TTL-expire. Established
  memories never decay mechanically — retirement is their only exit. Retirement
  (`hive_supersede` / `hive_prune` / `hive_write(replaces=)`) is agent-called but
  **machine-gated**: the server retires the target only when it verifies a qualifying machine
  signal itself — anchor drift at the canonical tip, hurt evidence from another identity or a
  verified outcome, a mechanical contradiction, or (for supersede) a near-duplicate successor.
  An unqualified call is a **benign no-op, never an error**: nothing is retired, the memory
  stays. `hive_flag` is advisory only and never qualifies the gate.

Every trust transition writes an audit row (machine-readable decision + actor).

## 4. Recall

`encode → dense cosine over the servable set in scope → absolute-relevance gate → abstain | serve`.

- **Scope.** `repos=["name"]` or `["name@branch"]` restricts to those repos (drift is judged
  at that branch tip; default = the repo's canonical ref); omitting `repos` is a **global**
  search. General (repo-less) memories are always candidates; `anchor_prefix` keeps only hits
  with an anchor under that path (general hits stay).
- The **gate** serves only if at least `k_min` candidates clear an absolute cosine floor
  `tau_serve`; otherwise it abstains. Empty / non-finite / any internal error → fail closed
  (abstain). A confident result is then decorrelated (`select_served`): the strictly
  higher-trust member of a near-duplicate pair wins, and same-trust cosine echoes collapse to
  the higher-similarity representative.
- A recall reply is `{reference_context: [hits…], abstained, state, top_cos}`. Each hit carries
  `trust` (`established` = outcome-verified on the canonical line | `provisional` = unverified),
  `ts`, `polarity` (`do`|`dont`|`neutral`), `kind`, `repos`, `anchors` (`[{repo, anchor}]`), and
  `drift` — the server-materialized staleness verdict, most severe across its anchors:
  `fresh | anchor_changed | anchor_missing | blast_radius_changed | branch_scoped |
  unverifiable | n/a` (`unverifiable` means not judged — never proof of freshness). Treat a
  drifted hit as **reference only**; a hit the server already knows is stale arrives with a
  remediation rider naming its options. Prefer higher-trust, newer hits; honor polarity.
- A recall may also carry a `conflicts` channel: ids-only notes about near-duplicate or opposing
  memories, to resolve via the retirement verbs. Recalled text is never returned as
  `instructions`.

## 5. The tools (MCP)

A connected agent gets eight `hive_*` tools. All are safe to call: the trust-changing verbs
carry no special field — retirement is adjudicated server-side by the machine gate.

| Tool | Signature | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `hive_recall` | `(query, repos?, anchor_prefix?)` | Retrieve servable memories in scope behind the abstention gate; returns reference context or abstains. |
| `hive_write` | `(text, replaces?, polarity?, kind?, anchors?, repos?, meta?)` | Save a memory that **serves now** as `provisional`; healed afterward by outcome/drift evidence. `replaces=<id>` retires the corrected memory only if the machine gate qualifies it (else the write lands and the envelope reports the retire as a no-op). |
| `hive_capture` | `(text, polarity?, kind?, anchors?, repos?, meta?)` | Leave a quarantined trace — the unclear-value tail; served only after independent demand (or a verified win) promotes it. |
| `hive_supersede` | `(loser, winner)` | Retire a stale memory in favor of its successor — machine-gated; unqualified ⇒ benign no-op. |
| `hive_prune` | `(episode_id)` | Bare-retire an incorrect/malicious/misleading memory — machine-gated; unqualified ⇒ benign no-op. |
| `hive_flag` | `(a, b, kind, winner?, resolution?)` | Record an **advisory** conflict/supersession note (`kind` ∈ `conflict`\|`supersedes`); never retires anything, never qualifies the gate. |
| `hive_outcome` | `(helped?, hurt?)` | Report which recalled ids helped/hurt your task. Evidence only — helped rows fuel promotion, hurt rows feed the retirement gate (a hurt row from another identity qualifies the target). |
| `hive_health` | `(include_gaps?, include_trends?, include_conflicts?, include_suspect_consensus?, include_stale_suspects?, include_census_health?, include_meta_versions?)` | Liveness/identity snapshot + optional KPIs and worklists. |

`kind` ∈ `{bug, gotcha, convention, design_choice, contract, dead_end, env_fact, note}`;
`polarity` ∈ `{do, dont, neutral}`. Both are carried-not-interpreted labels that ride every hit
but are **not** recall filters — recall matches the body text, so put the discriminating terms
there. Code binding is structured: `anchors=[{repo, anchor}]` — `repo` a **registered** repo
name (an unregistered name refuses the call), `anchor` the WHERE as `path/file.py::symbol`;
`repos=[...]` gives repo scope without a code anchor; neither = a general, fleet-wide memory.
The server mints fingerprints and judges drift per anchor — callers never supply fingerprint
material. `meta` is an optional opaque string map, served back verbatim, never interpreted.

## 6. Identity and the two doors

Identity is **per-agent-session**, resolved the same way on both doors:
`X-Hive-Agent-Id` header → the server-minted `Mcp-Session-Id` a conforming client echoes →
`local`. That per-session diversity is the promotion fuel; a fleet of K agents promotes
identically whether 1 or N engineers run it. Auth is a property of the **socket**, not a config
mode:

- **Loopback door** — `127.0.0.1:8765`, host-published, **tokenless**. For local agents on the
  trusted host. Never reachable remotely.
- **Tunnel door** — compose-internal `8766`, ngrok-forwarded, **token-required**. The only
  remote-reachable door, so a public caller is always bearer-gated by construction.

The bearer token **authenticates** the tunnel door; it is never the identity. There is no
`HIVE_AUTH__MODE` switch — a leftover one from an older config is ignored (a WARN, not a crash).

## 7. Setup — solo dev, one machine

Requirements: **Docker** + **Docker Compose v2**, and **Python 3.11+** on the host (for the
`hive` CLI, which drives Compose).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Hivemind-OSS/Hivemind.git hivemind && cd hivemind
pip install -e .          # installs the `hive` command (uninstalled: python3 -m hive.tools.cli)
hive up                   # build + start; zero-config; blocks until the daemon is healthy
hive repo add https://github.com/you/your-repo.git   # register each repo the fleet works on
```

Registration is operational: the row lands in the store's `repos` table and the sync daemon
picks it up on its next tick — no restart. `--token-env <ENVNAME>` names (never stores) the env
var holding a private repo's git token; unset, the fleet-default `HIVE_SYNC__TOKEN` applies.

Connect a local agent to the tokenless loopback door (example: Claude Code):

```bash
hive connect                                              # prints the ready-made line
claude mcp add --transport http hive http://localhost:8765/mcp
```

That is the whole setup. Agents are **thin, repo-agnostic MCP clients**: at connect the server
delivers its full usage contract through the MCP `initialize` instructions (every client
surfaces them) — fresh at every connect, so a session picks up a changed contract on reconnect.
Nothing is installed per agent, per project, or per device, and no rules-file edit exists.
Independent agent sessions on one machine each carry a distinct identity, so their shared
demand promotes good captures under the one anti-gaming rule with no flags to set.

## 8. Setup — a team connecting remotely

Loopback never leaves the host, so open exactly one door for teammates:

**Tunnel (recommended).** Free ngrok account, then in `.env`:

```bash
NGROK_AUTHTOKEN=...            # from the ngrok dashboard
NGROK_DOMAIN=your.ngrok.app    # your account's static domain (stable URL)
```

```bash
hive up --tunnel              # starts the ngrok sidecar; forwards https://<domain>/mcp
hive token alice-laptop       # mint a per-seat token (printed ONCE — hand over via a secret manager)
```

Each teammate registers the public URL with their seat token:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http hive https://<your-domain>/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <seat-token>"   # replace <seat-token> with the seat's token
```

TLS terminates at the ngrok edge, so the token is encrypted in transit. `hive up --tunnel`
fail-fasts if either ngrok secret is missing — a plain `hive up` never exposes anything.
Offboard a seat any time with `hive revoke <seat>` (its next request 401s).

**SSH alternative (no extra accounts):** `ssh -NL 8765:localhost:8765 you@host`, then the
localhost registration line from §7 works as-is. Never publish `0.0.0.0:8765` directly — a
bearer token over plain LAN HTTP is cleartext.

## 9. Operating it — best practices and KPIs

The store earns its value only if it is kept lean and current. The highest-leverage operator
moves:

- **Run agents as distinct sessions.** That diversity is what promotes good captures; with a
  single demand identity, nothing unvetted is ever served.
- **Register every repo the fleet works on.** Partitioning, census evidence, anchor
  fingerprints, and the drift verdicts on recall hits all key off the registry (`hive repo
  add`); an unregistered repo cannot be anchored to.
- **Keep it small; let unused memory expire.** Do not lengthen TTLs to hoard — expiry of
  unused, un-established memory is doing real work.
- **Seed and clean the served tier.** `hive_write` a good answer and it serves immediately;
  verified change outcomes on the canonical line establish it. Sweep the conflict and
  stale-suspect worklists into retirement calls — the machine gate makes calling safe, and
  retiring established falsehoods is the only thing that fights the dominant long-run decay.
- **Set the serve floor just below your true-match cosine.** Too high and the gate abstains on
  everything; recalibrate on your real query distribution.
- **`demand_m` is your coverage ↔ safety dial.** Raise it when a wrong answer is expensive,
  lower it when a missing answer wastes more time.

Watch these read-only signals over MCP on a fixed cadence (weekly suffices for a small team):

| Call | Tells you | Act on |
|---|---|---|
| `hive_health(include_trends=true)` | `confident_rate` + `demand_entropy` (7d deltas) — the only window into silent rot | `tau_serve`, `demand_m` |
| `hive_health(include_gaps=true)` | topics wanted but uncovered (each gap names the repos that asked) | `hive_write` the answers |
| `hive_health(include_conflicts=true)` | near-duplicate / contradicting memories + agent advisories, bucketed by repo and anchor | `hive_supersede` |
| `hive_health(include_suspect_consensus=true)` | provisionals promoted on thin *effective* independence | re-examine / retire |
| `hive_health(include_stale_suspects=true)` | servable memories in the blast radius of a breaking change | re-verify, then retire |
| `hive_health(include_census_health=true)` | per-repo census/sync state (days since the last change outcome, `last_tip`, `last_error`) | check the registry row / remote reachability |

## 10. Configuration knobs

All config has safe code defaults and is applied **only at boot** (restart to change; no live
reload). Override by copying `.env.example` to `.env` and setting `HIVE_<GROUP>__<FIELD>`.
Out-of-range values fail boot loudly; a key naming an unknown group or field is ignored with a
WARN (a leftover key from an older config is never a live switch). The load-bearing knobs (with
defaults):

| Env var | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `HIVE_RECALL__TAU_SERVE` | `0.70` | absolute-relevance serve floor (the never-hallucinate gate) |
| `HIVE_RECALL__K_MIN` | `1` | how many candidates must clear the floor to serve |
| `HIVE_AUTONOMY__DEMAND_M` | `3` | recall-misses needed to promote a quarantined memory |
| `HIVE_AUTONOMY__DEMAND_WINDOW_DAYS` | `14` | window over which demand is counted |
| `HIVE_AUTONOMY__QUARANTINE_TTL_DAYS` | `14` | how long an unused quarantined memory lives |
| `HIVE_AUTONOMY__PROVISIONAL_TTL_DAYS` | `45` | how long an unused provisional memory lives |
| `HIVE_AUTONOMY__VERIFIED_PROMOTION` | `true` | the verified-outcome rung out of quarantine; `false` makes it unreachable |
| `HIVE_CONFLICT__TAU` | `0.80` | near-duplicate cosine floor (serve-time dedup + conflict worklist) |
| `HIVE_SUSPECT_CONSENSUS__N_EFF_FRAC_MAX` | `0.5` | flags promotions on correlated (thin-independence) demand |
| `HIVE_SYNC__INTERVAL_S` | `60` | sync-daemon poll cadence in seconds (floor 5; an empty repo registry is an inert tick) |
| `HIVE_SECRET_SCAN__ENABLED` | `true` | the credential secret floor; `false` **loosens a safety gate** — bypasses the pre-persist scan so raw secrets are stored (logged at boot + in `hive_health`). |

Recalibrate the empirical floors (`tau_serve`, `conflict.tau`, `demand_m`) against your real
corpus and query distribution; the defaults are a conservative starting point, not a setpoint.

## 11. Agent working procedure (how an agent should use the memory)

This is the discipline the server delivers at connect; it is reproduced here so an integrator
knows what good agent behavior looks like:

- **Recall first, single-pointed.** Before building or re-deriving anything non-trivial, and on
  every error or surprise, recall the topic. Split a multi-part need into a **set of
  single-pointed queries** — one intent per query — and issue one `hive_recall` per intent; a
  bundled query dilutes toward the centroid and abstains. Scope with `repos=` /
  `anchor_prefix` when the need is repo-local; omit for global. Treat hits as reference,
  prefer `established` and newer, re-verify a drifted hit against the code, and never invent a
  memory when recall is empty.
- **Store per durable lesson: WHAT + WHERE + WHY.** Bind the WHERE as `anchors=[{repo,
  anchor}]` (registered repo + `path/file.py::symbol`) or `repos=[...]` for scope without a
  code anchor. **Write by default**: `hive_write` serves now as `provisional` and is healed by
  outcome and drift evidence; `hive_capture` is the unclear-value tail, quarantined until
  demand promotes it. Recall before writing to avoid duplicating or rivaling an existing
  memory. Worth storing: durable, reusable, non-obvious, evidence-grounded — never the
  obvious, transient, secret, or already-recallable; nothing clears the bar → store nothing.
- **Report outcomes at task end.** `hive_outcome(helped=[ids], hurt=[ids])` — evidence only;
  helped rows fuel promotion, hurt rows feed the retirement gate.
- **Maintain — machine-gated.** Stale (has a successor) → `hive_supersede` /
  `hive_write(replaces=)`; bad (incorrect/misleading) → `hive_prune`. The server retires only
  on a machine signal it verifies (drift, other-identity or verified hurt, contradiction);
  an unqualified call is a benign no-op, never an error — so calling is safe, and the gate
  decides. `hive_flag` records the semantic conflicts the near-dup scan can't see (advisory
  only). The `hive_health` worklists (conflicts, stale suspects, gaps) surface what needs
  resolving. An old `ts` is a staleness suspect, not a guarantee.

## 12. Day-2 operations

Everything runs through the `hive` CLI (it drives Docker Compose for you):

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `hive ui` | open the loopback operator dashboard in your browser — live status, seat mint/revoke, backup, non-blocking start/stop, tunnel activate/deactivate, restore from an in-volume backup (guarded, typed confirm), and the log tail (loopback-only, tokenless; no reset) |
| `hive status` | server health, tunnel state + URL, seat count |
| `hive logs [svc]` | follow the daemon (or `ngrok`) logs |
| `hive tokens` | list provisioned seat labels (never the tokens) |
| `hive token <seat>` | mint a per-seat token (printed once) |
| `hive revoke <seat>` | offboard a seat (next request → 401) |
| `hive repo add <url> [--name --branch --token-env]` | register a repo for the server-side census sync (picked up next tick; the registry stores env-var names, never a secret) |
| `hive repo remove <name>` | deregister a repo (stops feeding; the mirror is pruned next tick, memory scope kept) |
| `hive repos` | list registered repos (names + urls; never a secret) |
| `hive backup` | atomic snapshot of the store (manual; keeps the `backup_keep` most-recent) |
| `hive ingest <receipt.json>` | feed an unsigned census receipt's change outcome into the append-only evidence ledger (the manual escape hatch — the sync daemon feeds registered repos itself; idempotent; refused receipts write zero rows; `--post-merge --verdict pass\|fail --signal randomized\|canary\|none` for rollout outcomes) |
| `hive down` | stop the stack, preserve the data volume |
| `hive reset` | snapshot the store out to the host, then destroy + recreate it empty (recoverable; typed confirm) |
| `hive restore <snap>` | replace the live store from a snapshot (the inverse of reset; typed confirm) |
| `hive upgrade [--ref release]` | move the server to a vetted release ref — backup-gated, auto-rollback on failure |

**Security posture:** every memory is scanned for secrets before persistence (findings log rule
names, never the matched bytes; default refuse) — on by default, operator-disableable via
`HIVE_SECRET_SCAN__ENABLED=false` (logged at boot and surfaced in `hive_health`). The repo
registry stores no secret bytes — only the names of token env vars, resolved at tick time. The
image is hermetically offline. Only the loopback door is host-published; remote access is always
bearer-gated. Upgrading across schema generations is a single recoverable `hive reset` — it
snapshots the prior store to the host first, then recreates it empty (no in-place migration
ships; `hive restore` rolls back) — then `hive repo add` re-registers each repo.
